about.lede: I’m a product designer with more than 15 years of experience, including nearly 5 years leading high-performing design teams.

leadership.2.title: Kind + direct
leadership.2.body: Clear, direct communication keeps cross-functional teams working toward the same goal—and helps me understand what my team needs to succeed.
projects.ai-order-cloud.headline: Designing AI around the work—not the novelty.
projects.product-page-architecture.role: As the sole designer on this initiative, I helped diagnose the experience, synthesized behavioral and market evidence, proposed the new information architecture, and carried the direction through design exploration, prototyping, usability testing, and an A/B test.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.headlin: Powerful features for admins. Effortless engagement for everyone else.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.heading: Why it mattered.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.context: Recognition was one of our most-requested features and a natural extension of BambooHR’s “better together” story. As the first HRIS to offer it natively, our goal went beyond parity; we set out to create an exceptional experience for employees and admins.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.adminCh: I couldn’t remove all of the complexity from the admin experience, but I could make it easier to navigate. I organized the system around clear decisions, introduced complexity only when it was needed, and showed admins what would happen before they committed to a change.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.problem: When starting work on Recognition & Rewards, I had to consider both sides of the experience. Admins needed a clear way to set-up the program and keep it running with granular controls and easily accessed analytics. For employees, the challenge was participation: how could we make recognition a natural part of their day instead of another mundane task to remember?
about.body: I have a pragmatic approach to design—focus on human-centered design principles and results that drive business outcomes. Outside of work, I’m usually spending time with my family and our dogs. I love the desert, photography, and tinkering with 3D modeling/ printing. More than anything, I like building things. I’ve been fascinated by how things work for as long as I can remember, and that curiosity is what lead me to this career.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.outcome: Post-launch customer conversations also led us to ship more granular point allocations and automated birthday and anniversary recognition.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.highlig: The agent has entered the chat.
projects.product-page-architecture.draft: After roughly four weeks live, the results confirmed the hypothesis: customers didn't need fewer opportunities; they just needed them in the right order.

After a redesign by an external agency, upgrades and cross-sells had flattened. Site data showed the decline, but not the cause. I paired quantitative data with user sessions and heat maps from Quantum Metric. The synthesis revealed a clear pattern of hesitation and second guessing with each additional decision we put on the PDP.
Site data showed the decline. Research showed us why.
Our competitors repeated the same mistake.

We audited competitors in and out of market. Most in-category experiences stacked every cross-sell in the PDP, repeating the same overloaded pattern. Looking elsewhere surfaced stronger ways to sequence configuration and add-on decisions.
projects.ai-order-cloud.approach.0.body: I brought executives, department leaders, and key stakeholders together to identify where AI could create credible customer and business value. The workshop gave design a strategic role early enough to influence the premise, not just the interface.
projects.ai-order-cloud.decisionIntro.he: The principles that shaped the work.
about.headline: Curious by nature.
projects.product-page-architecture.draft: Keep momentum without removing the choices.
Every offer competed with the primary job to be done.

We launched the A/B test with only 10% of traffic to the new experience, then 50% and finally 100%. After four weeks live, the results confirmed our hypothesis: customers didn't need fewer choices; they just needed them in the right order.
This is example is purely for comparison with the redesigned PDP. The length of the page increase significantly, adding to the overall cognitive load.
While it was a step forward in regard to the UI, this new layout introduced more complexity and the cognative load started to drag conversion.
Retaining upsell opportunities without the cognitive overhead.
aiProjects.jobFinder.title: Signal: Personal Job Finder
aiProjects.jobFinder.description: If you've ever done a manual job search, you know its a mess out there. Signal pulls from public job feeds and employer sites, verifies and de-dupes the listings, then scores them for fit and confidence against my custom preferences. I can triage opportunities and track applications without losing the original listing.
aiProjects.iconFinder.description: I kept wasting time looking for the right icon. Icon Finder brings five libraries into one searchable catalog, connects everyday concepts to icon names, and ranks the results by relevance. Variants stay grouped, and the detail panel gives me the exact React import or, Unicode value (when available).
